title: Generic reducedness is invariant under characteristic-zero field extension
statement: Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $E/F$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $A$ be a commutative $F$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Give $E\otimes_F A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] the multiplication $(e\otimes a)(e\prime\otimes a\prime)=ee\prime\otimes aa\prime$. A prime ideal is minimal if it contains no strictly smaller prime ideal. A ring $T$ is called generically reduced if, for every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $T$, its localization $T_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is reduced, meaning that $x^m=0$ for an integer $m\geq1$ implies $x=0$. Then $A$ is generically reduced if and only if $E\otimes_F A$ is generically reduced. No finite generation, Noetherianity, algebraicity of $E/F$, or nonzero-algebra hypothesis is imposed; for the zero algebra the condition is vacuous.

source.place: Tags 00I4 (lemma-perfect-reduced) and 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down), combined generic-local consequence with faithfully flat descent as in the proof of 00HS; not a verbatim statement of either tag.

proof.text: Put $B=E\otimes_F A$ and $i:A\to B$, $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. If $A=0$, bilinearity makes every pure tensor zero, hence $B=0$; both spectra have no primes, so both generic-reducedness conditions are vacuous. We may therefore treat the case $A\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), bilinearity and generation by pure tensors; zero-ring case

proof.text: By field-extension base change, $A\to A\otimes_F E$ is faithfully flat. The switch $a\otimes e\mapsto e\otimes a$, with inverse $e\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes e$, identifies this with $i:A\to B$: the maps respect the bilinear relations and multiplication. Thus $i$ is faithfully flat and, in particular, flat.

For any minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$, let $\mathfrak p=i^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. This is prime since $i$ preserves products and $1$. It is minimal: if a prime $\mathfrak p_0$ were strictly smaller, going down for the flat map $i$ would give a prime $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak p_0$. Minimality forces $\mathfrak q_0=\mathfrak q$, contradicting their different contractions.

For any prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ set $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $C=E\otimes_F A_{\mathfrak p}$. Directly from the fraction and bilinearity relations there are inverse ring maps
$$C\longrightarrow i(S)^{-1}B,\quad e\otimes(a/s)\longmapsto (e\otimes a)/i(s),\qquad
 i(S)^{-1}B\longrightarrow C,\quad b/i(s)\longmapsto j(b)(1\otimes(s/1))^{-1},$$
where $j(e\otimes a)=e\otimes(a/1)$. For well-definedness, a fraction relation $u(as^{\prime}-a^{\prime}s)=0$ becomes the same relation with invertible $i(u)$; the tensor relations are bilinearity. The composites fix pure tensors and inverses of denominators, which generate the respective rings. In particular $j(b)=0$ if and only if $i(s)b=0$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 07JZ (definition-localization-module), and 00CX (lemma-tensor-product); explicit tensor-localization fraction calculation

proof.text:
Assume $A$ generically reduced, and take a minimal $\mathfrak q\subset B$. Its contraction $\mathfrak p$ is minimal by step 3, so $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is reduced by the hypothesis. The field $F$ is perfect because it has characteristic zero; $E$ is reduced because it is a field. The perfect-field reduced tensor theorem gives reducedness of $C=E\otimes_F A_{\mathfrak p}$. Now if $x=b/t\in B_{\mathfrak q}$ satisfies $x^n=0$, with $t
otin\mathfrak q$ and $n\ge1$, the fraction zero criterion gives $u
otin\mathfrak q$ with $ub^n=0$. Thus $j(ub)^n=j(u^{n-1}ub^n)=0$, and reducedness of $C$ gives $j(ub)=0$. Step 4 supplies $s
otin\mathfrak p$ with $i(s)ub=0$. Both $i(s)$ and $u$ avoid $\mathfrak q$, so their product does too, proving $b/t=0$ by the same fraction criterion. Hence $B$ is generically reduced.

Conversely assume $B$ generically reduced and fix a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$. Faithful flatness and surjectivity on spectra give a prime $\mathfrak q_0$ of $B$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. Choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak q_0$. Its contraction is a prime contained in $\mathfrak p$, hence equals $\mathfrak p$ by minimality. In particular $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is reduced by the assumption.

The localized map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat and local, since $i$ is flat and $i^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. A flat local map is faithfully flat. Apply universal injectivity to this map and the module $N=A_{\mathfrak p}$: under $N\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}B_{\mathfrak q}\cong B_{\mathfrak q}$, $a\otimes b\mapsto i_{\mathfrak q}(a)b$ with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, it says precisely that $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective. A nilpotent of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ maps to a nilpotent of the reduced ring $B_{\mathfrak q}$, hence to zero, and is therefore zero. This holds for every minimal $\mathfrak p$, proving generic reducedness of $A$.
